findings.title: Async functions called in forEach without await — DB updates may not complete
findings.body: In `handleCancelBooking.ts` lines 485-493, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await`. Since `forEach` does not wait for promises, the handler may return (and in a serverless environment, the process may be killed) before the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that sets `cancelled: true` completes. If the update doesn't persist, the CRON job will never see the reminder as cancelled, and the email will still be sent — reproducing the exact bug this PR aims to fix.

findings.title: Async functions called in forEach without await in requestReschedule
findings.body: In the `requestReschedule` mutation (lines 488-494), `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async functions called inside `forEach` without `await`. The mutation can return before the database updates (setting `cancelled: true`) complete. In a serverless environment the execution context may be recycled before these fire-and-forget promises resolve, leaving reminders uncancelled and causing emails to still be sent for rescheduled bookings.

findings.title: Async reminder cancellation in forEach is fire-and-forget during reschedule
findings.body: In `handleNewBooking.ts` lines 966-972, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` without `await`. Although wrapped in try/catch, the catch will never trigger because unhandled promise rejections from forEach callbacks don't propagate to the enclosing try/catch. More critically, the reschedule flow continues and returns a response before these DB updates complete, risking that `cancelled: true` is never persisted and the old reminders are still sent.

findings.title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders in batch
findings.body: The try/catch on line 53 wraps the entire for-loop that iterates over `remindersToCancel`. If `client.request` throws for any single reminder (e.g., network timeout, rate limit), the loop breaks and no subsequent reminders are cancelled. Their DB records are also not deleted. Since the CRON only targets reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, if the failure persists across CRON runs and the scheduled time passes, those emails will be sent despite being cancelled. Each reminder's SendGrid call should be individually try/caught to isolate failures.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves orphaned DB record
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true (lines 213-223), the function cancels the scheduled send in SendGrid and returns without deleting or marking the `workflowReminder` record in the database. Callers (reschedule in `handleNewBooking.ts`, workflow/step deletion in `workflows.tsx`) also do not delete the record. These orphaned records with `scheduled: true` and a stale `referenceId` will persist until the CRON's first `deleteMany` removes them after their `scheduledDate` passes, causing unbounded table growth for bookings far in the future.

findings.title: Unscheduled reminders query does not exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The query for unscheduled reminders (line 80-98) filters on `scheduled: false` but does not exclude `cancelled: true`. While in the current flow `cancelled` is only set on already-scheduled reminders (so `scheduled` would be true), there is no database constraint preventing a reminder from being both `cancelled: true` and `scheduled: false`. Adding `cancelled: { not: true }` (or `OR: [{ cancelled: false }, { cancelled: null }]`) would be a defensive safeguard against scheduling a cancelled reminder.

findings.title: Async reminder cancellation in forEach without await when editing workflow steps
findings.body: In the `update` mutation, `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => {...})` on line 574 calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` without awaiting the forEach itself. The mutation proceeds to create new reminders and returns a response before the old ones are marked as cancelled. If the execution context is recycled (serverless), the old reminders may never be marked cancelled and could still be sent by the CRON job.
